value.method: assisted use of background-check services to validate identity information

sources.quote: Chapman agrees and acknowledges that she did, in fact, perform the actions and have the knowledge ascribed to her below.
From in or around October 2020, until on or about October 26, 2023, Chapman, a U.S. national, conspired with certain overseas IT workers

the coconspirators used OBCS-1 to conduct more than 80 queries, to include criminal history reports and Social Security Number traces, of 57 U.S. persons’ identities in order to further their impersonation of these U.S. persons with U.S. employers.

notes: This is a plea-admitted factual basis, not an indictment-only allegation.
Victim identities, identity-document details, account selectors, and payment details are excluded.

sources.quote: Chapman received and hosted laptops issued by U.S. companies to the overseas IT workers in her U.S. residences (a “laptop farm”), so that the companies believed the workers to be located in the United States.
Chapman then installed AnyDesk and set up the laptop for remote work.

Chapman charged coconspirator overseas IT workers for “rent” and other fees for the services that she rendered in operating the laptop farm, to include logging into the U.S. companies’ laptops, connecting to the U.S. companies’ networks, downloading remote access software, connecting the overseas IT workers remotely to the laptops, providing technical support, laptop storage and shipping, and arranging for the transfer of payments.

notes: This conduct is admitted in the signed statement of offense.
Residential details, login credentials, device selectors, and raw communications are excluded.

sources.quote: Chapman and the coconspirator overseas IT workers impersonated U.S. persons, forging check endorsements and caused U.S. companies to make deposits in the names of individuals who were falsely associated with the transactions

after receiving fraudulent wages in her U.S. financial accounts, Chapman further transferred proceeds of the scheme to the coconspirator overseas IT workers. In exchange, Chapman charged monthly fees to the overseas IT workers for her services
The fees charged by Chapman totaled $176,850.00.

notes: This conduct and the aggregate fee total are admitted in the signed statement of offense.
No bank, account, check, victim, transfer, or transaction selector is retained.

sources.quote: through her LinkedIn page, and asked her to “be the U.S. face” of their company

notes: The public LinkedIn account itself was not resolved or authenticated.

sources.locator: PDF p. 1, Charges and Statutory Penalties
sources.quote: Your client agrees to plead guilty to Counts Two, Four, and Six in the Indictment, charging your client with Conspiracy to Commit Wire Fraud, Aggravated Identity Theft, and Conspiracy to Launder Monetary Instruments
pleaded guilty on Feb. 11 in the District of Columbia to conspiracy to commit wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and conspiracy to launder monetary instruments.

notes: The government agreed to seek dismissal of Counts 1, 3, 5, 7, and 8 after sentencing; the signed judgment records dismissal of all remaining counts.

sources.quote: a sentence of 70 to 87 months of incarceration on Counts Two and Six, plus an additional 24 months' incarceration on Count Four as required under 18 U.S.C. § 1028A(a)(1), for a total of 94 to 111 months of incarceration, followed by 3 years of supervised release

notes: This was the binding-agreement range presented to the court, not the sentence ultimately imposed; the signed judgment separately controls the 102-month disposition.

sources.quote: pleaded guilty to count(s) 2, 4 and 6
102 months, which consists of concurrent terms of 78 months as to Counts 2 and 6, and 24 months as to Count 4, which shall run consecutively to Counts 2 and 6.
36-months as to Counts 2 and 6, and 12 months as to Count 4 all to run concurrently.
Assessment $ 300.00
In addition to the 102-month prison term, U.S. District Court Judge Randolph D. Moss ordered Chapman to serve three years of supervised release

notes: Sentence was imposed July 24, 2025; the judgment was signed and filed July 30, 2025. These dates are not interchangeable.
The judgment initially deferred restitution.

sources.quote: which includes an amount totaling $284,666.92
A forfeiture money judgment in the amount of $176,850 is entered against the defendant and in favor of the United States.

sources.quote: The conspiracy impacted more than 300 U.S. companies, compromised more than 70 identities of U.S. persons, caused false information to be conveyed to DHS on more than 100 occasions, created false tax liabilities for more than 70 U.S. persons, and resulted in at least $17.1 million of revenue to be generated for the overseas IT workers.
Chapman helped North Korean IT workers obtain jobs at 309 U.S. companies
Chapman also shipped 49 laptops and other devices supplied by U.S. companies to locations overseas
More than 90 laptops were seized from Chapman’s home following the execution of a search warrant in October 2023.

notes: DOJ-reported conduct based on court documents; the plea and sentence are adjudicated separately.
Victim-company names, addresses, and device selectors are excluded.
